# i18n.x-default — a page of a multilingual hreflang set declares no x-default, or more than one

- **Check ID:** `i18n.x-default`
- **Default severity:** `warning`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** Google rel=alternate hreflang
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/i18n-x-default.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/i18n.x-default.md`](../i18n.x-default.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

A page of a multilingual hreflang set declares no `x-default` entry, or declares more than one.

## Why it matters

`x-default` is the entry that says which page to use when the visitor's language is not among the alternates: the language-selection page, or the default-language page. Without it, search engines and agents pick a language for the visitor, often the wrong one, and a person landing on a page they cannot read has no declared way out. Declaring it twice is its own failure: the alternate set then has two competing fallback pages, and engines stop trusting the set as a whole.

## What it checks

The check runs only on a **multilingual site**: one whose `rel="alternate" hreflang=...` declarations cover two or more distinct language codes, compared without regard to case so `DE` and `de` are the same language. Entries pointing outside this build count as declarations; they are never fetched. A site with a single language declares no set to fall back from, so nothing is reported.

Within such a site, a page **takes part in the hreflang set** when it declares at least one `hreflang` alternate itself (an `x-default` entry is not a language and does not count) or when another page names it as a translation, meaning the other page's alternate `href` resolves to it in the built site. Every participating page needs **exactly one** `<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="...">`:

- **No x-default** (warning): reported once for the page, at its `<head>`. The fix hint offers the tag with a placeholder `href`, because only a human knows which page is the site's fallback.
- **More than one x-default** (warning): also reported at the page's `<head>`, listing the `href` values that compete.

Pages outside the set stay silent, as does a page whose alternate entries carry no `href` (an entry without a target declares nothing usable, and `i18n.hreflang` ignores it too). The `hreflang="x-default"` value itself is matched case-insensitively. `<link>` elements in HTTP `Link` headers are not read, and nothing leaves the build: the whole rule is settled from the HTML on disk. What the single `x-default` entry points at is not verified here — `i18n.hreflang` checks the language entries only — so a fallback page missing from the build is a gap in both checks.

## How to fix

```html
<!-- before: /de/index.html is in an en/de hreflang set and declares no fallback -->
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="de" href="/de/index.html">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="/index.html">
<!-- after: one x-default entry, pointing at the language-selection page -->
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="de" href="/de/index.html">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="/index.html">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="/index.html">
```

Point `x-default` at the page that offers the language choice, or at your default-language page when there is no chooser — the same target on every page of the set. Where a generator emits the tags, add the entry to its i18n configuration (for example the theme's language list) so every page gets it, rather than editing the built HTML. Delete the surplus entries when a page declares `x-default` more than once; keeping one is enough.

## Options

None.

## Standards

- [Google: Tell Google about localized versions of your page](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions) (the `x-default` value)
- [`i18n.hreflang`](i18n.hreflang.md), the sibling check for the language entries themselves
